cubes.name: staff_directory
cubes.title: Staff Directory
cubes.description:
Open staff directory — roster, employment history, and work-contact info. One row per employee x employment period — a contiguous window during which status, job, worker type, org unit, and location all held simultaneously — with point-in-time manager context. Use for the staff roster, drill-down, and individual investigations. Contains no personal or sensitive data (personal contact, DOB, demographics) — see staff_pii for those fields.
Always apply a date filter. Without one, each employment period fans out to one row per calendar day in its effective range. For a current roster, filter dates to today; for headcount over time, filter a date range or month-ends. Filter is_primary_position = true to count each person once; status_name = 'Active' filters to active employees (excludes Leave). Use count_employees (count_distinct on staff_key) for headcounts.

cubes.name: staff_pii
cubes.title: Staff Pii
cubes.description:
Sensitive staff PII — personal contact info, date of birth, and demographics — split out of the open staff directory (see staff_directory). One row per employee x employment period; always apply a date filter or each period fans out to one row per calendar day in its effective range. Filter is_primary_position = true and status_name = 'Active' to see each current employee once.
Row-level access is remit-scoped: a viewer only sees rows for staff within their location/department remit (added in Task 5's row_level policy). job_function_level, job_function_code, and department_group are exposed here because the remit filter matches on them; abbreviation and region_key are exposed because the remit filter also scopes by location. Those three role attributes are the viewed staff member's CURRENT role (from dim_staff_cube_access), not the value per historical period — so the remit gate is person-level, not period-accurate.

cubes.name: student_assessment_scores_view
cubes.title: Student Assessment Scores View
cubes.description: Assessment scores across internal Illuminate interims, NJ/FL state assessments, and vendor benchmarks (i-Ready, DIBELS, STAR) — row-level (one row per student x assessment x administration x response type) and aggregate breakdowns in a single view. pct_proficient (mastery rate) is the source-agnostic headline; scale_score is null for internal rows and percent_correct is null for state and vendor rows. response_type / response_type_code carry the standard/skill breakdown (Illuminate only). State and vendor administrations have no single administered date, so the Date members (academic_year, academic_year_label, date_day, month_number, month_name) resolve for every source but are scoped by different dates per source: the administration date for Illuminate/college, the student's completion (test) date for state/vendor. A cross-source date cut (e.g. "scores in May") therefore mixes those two date concepts. Contains direct student identifiers — see access_policy for PII gating.

measures.name: student_assessment_scores_view.count_scores
measures.title: Student Assessment Scores View Count Scores
measures.description: Scored-response count. COUNT(*) over the unique PK (assessment_score_key) — additive, so pre-aggregations roll it up to any grain.

measures.name: student_assessment_scores_view.count_students
measures.title: Student Assessment Scores View Count Students
measures.description: Distinct students (per student-year) with a score in the filtered slice. Exact count_distinct — non-additive, so a rollup pre-aggregation cannot re-aggregate it to a coarser grain; switch to count_distinct_approx (HLL) if/when this is pre-aggregated and an approximate distinct is acceptable.

measures.name: student_assessment_scores_view.pct_proficient
measures.title: Student Assessment Scores View Pct Proficient
measures.description: Proficiency/mastery rate — proficient scores / total scores. The headline, source-agnostic metric (the only score measure comparable across the incompatible scales of internal vs state assessments). Built from additive primitives (_sum_proficient / count_scores) so pre-aggregations roll it up to any grain.

measures.name: student_assessment_scores_view.pct_proficient_formative
measures.title: Student Assessment Scores View Pct Proficient Formative
measures.description: Proficiency rate across all formative module types (Quick Assessments, Multiple-Choice Quick Questions, and Constructed Response Questions). CRQ is included and also available as the standalone pct_proficient_crq measure. Built from additive primitives so pre-aggregations roll it up.

measures.name: student_assessment_scores_view.pct_proficient_crq
measures.title: Student Assessment Scores View Pct Proficient Crq
measures.description: Proficiency rate for Constructed Response Questions (CRQ) across all regions. CRQ is a subset of pct_proficient_formative. Built from additive primitives so pre-aggregations roll it up.

measures.name: student_assessment_scores_view.avg_percent_correct
measures.title: Student Assessment Scores View Avg Percent Correct
measures.description: Grain: recomputes at any query grain, but meaningful only within a single subject/standard — pooling percent-correct across assessments is a silent-failure trap (numerically valid, semantically meaningless). Average percent correct, internal-effective (null for state), built from additive primitives so pre-aggregations roll it up.

measures.name: student_assessment_scores_view.avg_scale_score
measures.title: Student Assessment Scores View Avg Scale Score
measures.description: Grain: recomputes at any query grain, but meaningful only within a single assessment source/subject/grade — scale scores are not comparable across sources, so pooling them is a silent-failure trap (numerically valid, semantically meaningless). Average scale score, built from additive primitives so pre-aggregations roll it up.

cubes.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view
cubes.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View
cubes.description:
Student enrollment and attendance on one daily surface — one row per student per calendar day they were enrolled. Enrollment decides which rows exist and attendance is joined on top, so a day with no recorded attendance is still a row. Contains direct student identifiers — see access_policy for PII gating.
count_students is a distinct-student count over whatever slice is queried. Leave the date open for ever-enrolled over a range; pin it to one date for a point-in-time headcount as of that date. There is no anchor filter and none is needed — break days carry a row, so a weekend or a holiday resolves exactly like a school day. Filter is_in_session_day = true for anything that should count school days only.
Filter attendance_date, not dates_date_day, for a single date or a date range. The two return identical rows, but attendance_date compiles to a predicate on the fact's own partitioning column and prunes the scan, while dates_date_day compiles to a predicate on dim_dates and leaves the whole 29.6M-row fact to be read. Use the dates_* members for grouping and for academic-year, month, or week-of questions, where they are the only path.
For ADA use the avg_daily_attendance measure rather than rebuilding the ratio from raw dimensions — it scopes both sides to full membership days with a recorded attendance value, and a hand-rolled SUM(attendance_value) / SUM(membership_value) counts days that were never recorded. Never average a per-row ratio either way. attendance_value (0.0 to 1.0) is the fractional attendance contribution; membership_value (0.0 to 1.0) is the school's claim on the student that day, split across schools if dual-enrolled, and zero on every break day; present_weight equals attendance_value but tardies count 0.67. attendance_category is the coarse rollup (Present, Absent, Tardy, In-School Suspension, Out-of-School Suspension) and is null when no attendance was recorded, which means unknown rather than present; attendance_code is the raw SIS code.
This view answers day-level and point-in-time questions. Every measure on it is day-weighted — a ratio of summed day counts, additive over any date range you slice it by. That weighting is the dividing line with student_attendance_enrollment_periods_view, whose measures are student-weighted: they count students who crossed a threshold cumulatively by period end, and cannot be rebuilt from these daily rows. So chronic absence, ADA tier mix and truancy rates live on that view and not this one, and every attendance-rate measure, ADA included, lives on this one and not that one. A question that wants both — chronic absence and ADA by region this month — is two queries, one per view. Do not substitute a tier percentage for an attendance rate.
Every rate on this view divides by count_students, which counts students with recorded attendance. No minimum-day floor applies -- one measured day is enough -- but a student whose attendance was never recorded is outside both the numerator and the denominator. Population and denominator are the same number, so they cannot drift apart and an unmeasured student cannot pull a rate down.

measures.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.count_students
measures.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Count Students
measures.description:
Distinct students with recorded attendance in the queried slice, and the denominator for every rate here. Enrollment decides which rows exist, by entry and exit dates rather than status, but a student whose attendance was never recorded is excluded — a day nobody measured cannot support a headcount or a rate, and counting it once inflated every denominator it reached. Population and denominator are therefore the same number and cannot drift apart.
Leave the date open for an ever-enrolled count over a range; pin attendance_date to a single date for a point-in-time headcount as of that date. Use attendance_date rather than dates_date_day, because it prunes the fact's date partition and dates_date_day does not. No anchor filter is needed or available — the fact carries a row for every calendar day a student was enrolled, break days included, so a weekend or holiday resolves the same as a school day.

 For students served across a whole period
use student_attendance_enrollment_periods_view.count_students, which answers a different question from enrolled on a given date.

measures.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.avg_daily_attendance
measures.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Avg Daily Attendance
measures.description: Average Daily Attendance (ADA) — attendance value summed over full membership days, divided by the count of those days. Days with no recorded attendance value are excluded from both numerator and denominator, matching the attendance dashboard; counting them in the denominator alone would report them as absences.

measures.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.pct_tardy
measures.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Pct Tardy
measures.description:
Percentage of present days where the student was tardy (tardy days / present days). Absent days and days with no recorded attendance value are excluded from both numerator and denominator.
Date filter behavior: filtering to a single date returns that day's tardy rate only. For a cumulative YTD rate as of a given date, use a date range from the start of the academic year (e.g. 2025-07-01 through the target date).

measures.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.pct_ontime
measures.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Pct Ontime
measures.description:
Percentage of present days where the student arrived on time (on-time days / present days). Complement of pct_tardy. Absent days and days with no recorded attendance value are excluded from both numerator and denominator.
Date filter behavior: filtering to a single date returns that day's on-time rate only. For a cumulative YTD rate as of a given date, use a date range from the start of the academic year (e.g. 2025-07-01 through the target date).

measures.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.count_absent_days
measures.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Count Absent Days
measures.description: Total number of absence days (sum of is_absent). Filtered to membership_value > 0 to exclude non-enrollment days while retaining partial-membership days (dual-enrolled students). Not restricted to membership_value = 1 — partial days count as absences too.

measures.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.count_chronically_absent
measures.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Count Chronically Absent
measures.description: Students at Tier 3 or Tier 4 as of the pinned date. Pin attendance_date. No minimum-membership-day floor is applied, so early in an academic year this counts students judged on very few days -- show count_students beside it. Counts distinct students, so a student who changed schools counts once at each school when grouped by school and once overall when not; the cumulative position it reads accumulates per student across the change rather than resetting.

measures.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.pct_chronically_absent
measures.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Pct Chronically Absent
measures.description: Share of students at Tier 3 or Tier 4 as of the pinned date. Denominator is count_students, every student in the queried slice. No minimum-membership-day floor applies. Numerator and denominator share the same population, so a student whose attendance was never recorded is outside both and cannot pull the rate down.  Pin attendance_date, and show count_students beside this: a rate over students with only a few membership days each is volatile, not wrong.

measures.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.count_truants
measures.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Count Truants
measures.description:
Students meeting regional truancy criteria as of the pinned date. Miami: 15+ absences in a 90-day rolling window. NJ regions: projected absences reach 50+ for the year. Pin attendance_date.
Neither regional rule requires a minimum membership-day count. Miami's is self-limiting -- 15 absences implies at least 15 membership days -- while the NJ projection can fire in a student's first days, so early in an academic year this runs high.

measures.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.pct_truant
measures.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Pct Truant
measures.description:
Share of students meeting regional truancy criteria as of the pinned date. Denominator is count_students, every student in the queried slice. No minimum-membership-day floor applies. Numerator and denominator share the same population, so a student whose attendance was never recorded is outside both and cannot pull the rate down.
 Truancy has no eligibility concept
in either regional rule. Pin attendance_date.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.is_in_session_day
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Is in Session Day
dimensions.description: Whether school was in session for this student's school on this day. False on a break day, which carries enrollment but no attendance and a membership_value of zero. Filter to true for anything that should only consider school days; leave it open for enrollment questions, which is what makes a point-in-time count resolve on a weekend or holiday.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.attendance_date
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Attendance Date
dimensions.description: This day's calendar date, read from the fact rather than through the dates join. Prefer it over dates_date_day for any single-date or date-range filter: it compiles to a predicate on fct_student_attendance_enrollment_daily' own date_key, which is the table's partitioning column, whereas a dates_date_day filter lands on dim_dates and leaves the whole fact to be scanned. Both return the same rows.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.attendance_code
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Attendance Code
dimensions.description: Attendance identifier set by school. Examples Tardy, Absent, etc.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.attendance_category
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Attendance Category
dimensions.description: Coarse attendance category derived from the is_* flags with priority ordering (suspension > absent > tardy > present). Values: Out-of-School Suspension, In-School Suspension, Absent, Tardy, Present. Use this column for GROUP BY in BI tools; use the raw attendance_code for specific-code drill-down.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.attendance_value
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Attendance Value
dimensions.description: Daily attendance value — a real number, typically a fraction of 1 where 1 is a full attendance day. Used with membership_value to compute ADA. Precision depends on the source SIS's attendance mode (full-day vs period-level vs day-part); see source_model for provenance.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.membership_value
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Membership Value
dimensions.description: The amount of a student's membership this school claims. If a student attends more than one school each one will only be able to claim a certain portion of the membership. The largest number for this will usually be 1 and fractions expressed as decimals. Like .5 or .25.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.present_weight
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Present Weight
dimensions.description: Weighted presence value. 0.67 for tardy (T-prefix codes), otherwise equals attendance_value. Fractional by design — not a 0/1 flag.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.is_absent
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Is Absent
dimensions.description: 1 if the student was absent, 0 if present. Sum-friendly flag.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.is_tardy
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Is Tardy
dimensions.description: 1 if the student was tardy (T-prefix attendance code), 0 otherwise.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.is_ontime
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Is Ontime
dimensions.description: 1 if the attendance code is not a T-prefix tardy code, 0 if tardy. Note: this is 1 for absent days as well as on-time present days — use pct_ontime for an on-time rate that correctly excludes absent days.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.is_oss
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Is Oss
dimensions.description: 1 if the student received out-of-school suspension on this date (OS, OSS, OSSP, SHI codes), 0 otherwise.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.is_iss
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Is Iss
dimensions.description: 1 if the student received in-school suspension on this date (S, ISS codes), 0 otherwise.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.is_suspended
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Is Suspended
dimensions.description: 1 if the student was suspended (any type) on this date. Union of is_oss and is_iss codes.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.is_truant
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Is Truant
dimensions.description:
Day-level flag: TRUE if the student met regional truancy criteria as of this date. Miami: 15+ absences in a 90-day rolling window. NJ regions: projected absences reach 50+ for the year.
Grain trap — this flag is re-stamped on every daily row, and the NJ projection moves as the year progresses. Filtering it over a date range therefore counts students truant on ANY day in the range, not a period-end snapshot, and the count runs high: early in an academic year it runs high several-fold, because one absence in the first days projects past 50 on a one-day denominator. Use this dimension for day-level drill-down (which days was a student flagged), and take the period-end truancy count and rate from student_attendance_enrollment_periods_view's count_truants / pct_truant.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.n_membership_days_ytd
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View N Membership Days Ytd
dimensions.description: Membership days accumulated from the start of the academic year at this school, through and including this date. Counts only days with a recorded attendance value, so a day whose register was never taken raises neither this nor n_present_days_ytd. Unchanged across break days, because a break day contributes zero -- so this resolves on a weekend or a holiday with the value from the last school day.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.n_present_days_ytd
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View N Present Days Ytd
dimensions.description: Attendance accumulated from the start of the academic year at this school, through and including this date, over the same days n_membership_days_ytd counts. Divide by n_membership_days_ytd for one student's cumulative ADA as of this date. That is a per-student figure -- for a population ADA over a date range use avg_daily_attendance, which sums both sides over the slice and is not the same number.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.ada_tier
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Ada Tier
dimensions.description:
Cumulative ADA band as of this date. Tier 1 at 95% and above, Tier 2 strictly above 90.0%, Tier 3 from 80% through 90.0% inclusive, Tier 4 below 80%. Null when the student has no membership days yet.
Exactly 90.0% is Tier 3, and therefore chronically absent. Evaluated on accumulated counts cross-multiplied against each other, never on an averaged float. Computed once in fct_student_attendance_enrollment_daily; student_attendance_enrollment_periods_view reads the same column at period end rather than recomputing it, so the two views cannot disagree.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.is_chronically_absent
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Is Chronically Absent
dimensions.description: Whether ada_tier is Tier 3 or Tier 4 as of this date. Derived from ada_tier, never recomputed, so the flag and the tier cannot drift apart. A student with only a handful of membership days still carries a tier -- show count_students beside any rate built on this.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.dates_academic_year
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Dates Academic Year
dimensions.description: KIPP academic year (July start). The calendar year in which the academic year begins (e.g., 2025 for the 2025-26 school year). For filtering by year, prefer academic_year_label (the unambiguous "2025-2026" string form) over this integer.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.dates_academic_year_label
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Dates Academic Year Label
dimensions.description: Full span label for the academic year (e.g. "2025-2026" for the year beginning July 2025). Use this as the canonical filter surface when querying by year — it is unambiguous regardless of SY vs. start-year notation. academic_year 2025 = academic_year_label "2025-2026" = SY26. The integer academic_year is retained for sort/group/math only.

dimensions.name: student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.dates_date_day
dimensions.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Daily View Dates Date Day
dimensions.description:
Timestamp cast of date_key. Required by Cube for date dimension joins.
Grain: a year granularity on this dimension buckets on the CALENDAR year, not the KIPP academic year — silent-failure trap. Asking for year granularity here splits every academic year across two buckets and answers a different question with no error. Measured on student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view: distinct students by year granularity returns 12,847 / 13,163 / 10,726 where the academic-year answer is 10,158 / 10,849 / 11,260. Group by academic_year_label (or academic_year) for anything school-year-shaped, and reserve this dimension's granularities for day, week, month and quarter.

cubes.name: student_attendance_enrollment_periods_view
cubes.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Periods View
cubes.description:
Student counts and rates for a period — chronic absence and ADA tier mix as of the period's last membership day, truancy on any membership day in it. Use this view for "how many students crossed a line" questions (chronic absence rate this year, ADA tier mix this month, truancy trend by week).
Every measure here is student-weighted: it counts students against a threshold they reached cumulatively by period end. There is no attendance-rate measure on this view and no ADA — those are day-weighted and live on student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view, which is also where day-level questions belong (was a student absent on a given date, a calendar heatmap, day-of-week patterns). This view carries pre-computed period snapshots; that one carries the row-level daily record. A question that wants both a rate-of-students and an attendance rate is two queries, one per view: do not substitute pct_chronically_absent or pct_tier_1_2 for ADA, and do not rebuild chronic absence from daily rows.
Set period_type to year, month, or week to select the grain and group by period_start_date. No anchor filter is needed or accepted — the row already carries the period's value, so there is nothing to pin it to: a single-date filter narrows which periods you get back rather than selecting a point in time within one. A row exists only for a period in which the student had a membership day at that school, so a withdrawn student stops appearing rather than carrying forward, and a trend's denominator shifts between points.
Truancy is the one measure here that is not read as of period end. Chronic absence and ADA tier only ever accumulate, so their last-day reading is their high-water mark; truancy is a status that turns on and off within a period, so count_truants and pct_truant count a student who met the criteria on any membership day in it. For truancy as of one specific date, pin attendance_date on student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view instead.
No minimum-membership-day floor is applied to any rate on this view. Every rate divides by the students who have at least one recorded attendance day in the period, so an early period reports a rate over students judged on very few days each — a student who misses one of their first four days sits at 75% ADA and counts as chronically absent. That makes the first weeks of an academic year volatile rather than wrong. Always display count_students alongside any rate measure on this view.
Paterson's presence-derived measures (ada_tier, pct_chronically_absent, truancy) carry a known upstream uncertainty from incomplete PowerSchool attendance-conversion items (#4193), unquantified as of AY2025; count_students is unaffected. The conversion items were never captured at the time, so this is unlikely to be backfilled.
Every rate on this view divides by count_students, which counts students with recorded attendance. No minimum-day floor applies -- one measured day is enough -- but a student whose attendance was never recorded is outside both the numerator and the denominator. Population and denominator are the same number, so they cannot drift apart and an unmeasured student cannot pull a rate down.

measures.name: student_attendance_enrollment_periods_view.count_students
measures.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Periods View Count Students
measures.description:
Distinct students with recorded attendance at any point in the period, and the denominator for every rate here. No minimum-day floor applies -- one measured day is enough -- but a student whose attendance was never recorded is excluded, because a day nobody measured cannot support a headcount or a rate. Population and denominator are therefore the same number and cannot drift apart.
Counts distinct students, so a student who changed schools mid-period counts once at each school when grouped by school and once overall when not: the school is answerable for the days the student was there, while the student is one student.
This is a served-during-the-period count, a different question from enrolled on a given date — for that, pin the date on student_attendance_enrollment_daily_view.
This is the denominator for every rate on this cube — chronic absence, both ADA-tier shares, and truancy. No rate here applies a minimum-membership-day floor, so show this count beside any of them for an early period, where the rate is computed over students judged on very few days.

measures.name: student_attendance_enrollment_periods_view.count_chronically_absent
measures.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Periods View Count Chronically Absent
measures.description: Student-school records with cumulative ADA at or below 90.0% (ada_tier Tier 3 or Tier 4) as of period_end_date. Same distinct-student counting as count_students, and no minimum-membership-day floor. The tier itself accumulates per student across a school change, so a transferring student arrives already carrying their position.

measures.name: student_attendance_enrollment_periods_view.pct_chronically_absent
measures.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Periods View Pct Chronically Absent
measures.description:
Chronic absence rate. Denominator is count_students, every student in the queried slice. No minimum-membership-day floor applies. Numerator and denominator share the same population, so a student whose attendance was never recorded is outside both and cannot pull the rate down.
So an early period reports a rate over students judged on very few days: a student who misses one of their first four days sits at 75% ADA and counts as chronically absent. Always display count_students alongside this rate, and treat the first weeks of an academic year as volatile rather than wrong.

measures.name: student_attendance_enrollment_periods_view.pct_tier_1_2
measures.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Periods View Pct Tier12
measures.description:
Percentage of students with cumulative ADA strictly above 90.0% (Tier 1 or Tier 2) as of period_end_date. Tier 2 is strictly above 90.0%; Tier 3 includes exactly 90.0%.
Denominator is count_students, every student in the queried slice. No minimum-membership-day floor applies. Numerator and denominator share the same population, so a student whose attendance was never recorded is outside both and cannot pull the rate down.

measures.name: student_attendance_enrollment_periods_view.pct_tier_3
measures.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Periods View Pct Tier3
measures.description:
Percentage of students with cumulative ADA from 80% through 90.0% inclusive (Tier 3) as of period_end_date. Tier 2 is strictly above 90.0%; Tier 3 includes exactly 90.0%.
Denominator is count_students, every student in the queried slice. No minimum-membership-day floor applies. Numerator and denominator share the same population, so a student whose attendance was never recorded is outside both and cannot pull the rate down.

measures.name: student_attendance_enrollment_periods_view.count_truants
measures.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Periods View Count Truants
measures.description:
Student-school records meeting regional truancy criteria on any membership day in the period. Miami: 15+ absences in a 90-day rolling window. NJ regions: projected absences reach 50+ for the year. Same distinct-student counting grain as count_students.
This is the one measure here not read as of period_end_date -- see is_truant for why, and for how to get a single-date reading instead.
No eligibility floor is applied here. Neither the Miami nor the NJ truancy rule requires a minimum membership-day count, so any such floor belongs inside is_truant on the fact, not in this measure or its denominator. Miami's rule is already self-limiting — 15 absences implies at least 15 membership days. NJ's is not: its projection can fire in a student's first days, so early-period counts run high. At year grain the effect is nil (AY2025 NJ: 233 truant either way); at month grain it is concentrated in the first weeks (2025-08: 550 rows here that an eligibility floor would have reported as zero). Show count_students beside this measure for any early period.

measures.name: student_attendance_enrollment_periods_view.pct_truant
measures.title: Student Attendance Enrollment Periods View Pct Truant
measures.description:
Percentage of students meeting regional truancy criteria on any membership day in the period. Denominator is count_students, every student in the queried slice. No minimum-membership-day floor applies. Numerator and denominator share the same population, so a student whose attendance was never recorded is outside both and cannot pull the rate down. Truancy has no eligibility concept in either the Miami or the NJ rule.
Any minimum-membership-day condition would belong inside is_truant on the fact, which keeps this denominator correct through a later change to that definition. See count_truants for how the numerator behaves early in an academic year.

dimensions.description: Selects the grain: year, month, or week. Week is the PowerSchool school week (not a clean Monday-Sunday ISO grid). Each period_type produces exactly one pre-computed row per eligible student per period — no anchor filter is needed or accepted. The dates join is on period_end_date_key, so a single-date filter selects the periods that ended on that date rather than pinning a point in time within one.

Pin count_students to this for a period headcount the way Topline's Total Enrollment is meant to read, rather than to the calendar start, which reports nobody for a week whose Monday was not in session and a full roster for a week that had not begun. Equals the calendar start whenever that day was in session.

cubes.name: student_section_enrollments_view
cubes.title: Student Section Enrollments View
cubes.description: Student section enrollments — row-level (one row per student x section enrollment) and aggregate headcounts in a single view. Use for per-teacher class rosters (filter to a lead teacher) and section drill-down. count_students is a distinct-student headcount, correct per teacher — grouped by lead teacher it answers "how many students does this teacher teach?". Contains direct student identifiers — see access_policy for PII gating.

measures.name: student_section_enrollments_view.count_students
measures.title: Student Section Enrollments View Count Students
measures.description: Distinct students with a section enrollment in the filtered slice. Answers "how many students does this teacher teach?" when grouped by the lead teacher. count_distinct on the student, so it is fan-safe.

dimensions.name: student_section_enrollments_view.student_section_enrollment_key
dimensions.title: Student Section Enrollments View Student Section Enrollment Key
dimensions.description: Surrogate key (cc_dcid, _dbt_source_project). Primary key — one row per CC record.

dimensions.name: student_section_enrollments_view.student_enrollment_key
dimensions.title: Student Section Enrollments View Student Enrollment Key

dimensions.description: KIPP academic year (July start) the section enrollment falls in. The calendar year the academic year begins (e.g., 2025 for 2025-26). This is the canonical academic_year for the assessment-scores views.

dimensions.title: Student Section Enrollments View Entry Date

dimensions.name: student_section_enrollments_view.exit_date
